holidays.name: International Quirkyalone Day
holidays.description: Valentine's Day for people who love being independent. It celebrates those who prefer to stay true to themselves over settling for just anyone, whether they're single, dating, or in a relationship. Quirkyalones tend to be romantic, but they refuse to feel bad about flying solo.
holidays.origin: Writer Sasha Cagen coined the term 'quirkyalone' around 2000. She started the day as an alternative to Valentine's Day, one that doesn't make anyone feel left out.
holidays.funFact: Cagen's idea grew into a 2004 book, Quirkyalone: A Manifesto for Uncompromising Romantics, and fans have thrown Quirkyalone parties in cities around the world.

holidays.name: National Ferris Wheel Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the giant rotating wheel that has carried thrill-seekers and first dates skyward for over a century. Take a ride, admire the view, and appreciate a machine that goes in circles but always feels like progress.
holidays.origin: The day honors George Washington Gale Ferris Jr., the engineer who built the original Ferris wheel, which debuted at the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago. He was born on February 14, 1859.
holidays.funFact: The first Ferris wheel stood about 264 feet tall and was built to rival the Eiffel Tower, which had wowed visitors at the 1889 Paris fair.

holidays.name: National Cream-Filled Chocolates Day
holidays.description: A day for biting into a chocolate and finding a soft, creamy surprise inside. It suits the day of love and candy hearts well, whether you favor caramel, fondant, or fruity creams.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It lands on Valentine's Day, the biggest chocolate-gifting day of the year.
holidays.funFact: Americans buy millions of pounds of chocolate each Valentine's season, and filled assortments are among the most popular gift boxes.
